standard.title: Arts importance for communities
standard.description: explore how and why the arts are important for people and communities
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior Drama curriculum. Students have personal experience of arts in their lives — songs, stories, performances — but have not yet been prompted to consider why people make and share arts works.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how and why the arts — including drama — are important for people and communities.

nodes.label: Noticing arts in life and community
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify arts works they have experienced in their lives and describe what they noticed.
nodes.minimum_width: Student names at least one arts experience from their life (song, story, dance, game) and says something about it.
nodes.typical_width: Students identify arts works and experiences from school, home and community (songs, animations, dances, drama); they share ideas and feelings about those works with peers and teachers.
wider: Students explore arts from different cultures in their community — including cultural dances, songs or stories — noticing how these carry different meanings for different people

Students engage with First Nations Australians' perspectives on why the arts matter for connecting to people, culture and Country/Place, using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot yet identify or recall an arts experience, they have no grounded example from which to explore the 'why'; the second node — understanding purpose and meaning — cannot proceed without a concrete referent.

response_modes.reason: Cast the net widely: songs, animations, games, performances at community events all count. Students who don't recognise formal theatre often strongly identify with games or songs — breadth of examples makes this accessible to all.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of cultural arts experiences Foundation students bring is very wide; explicitly recognising and valuing diverse community arts contexts enriches shared understanding of why arts matter.
success_criteria: Student names at least one arts experience from their own life
Student can say something (however simple) about what they noticed or felt

nodes.label: Why arts matter for people and communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain a simple reason why an arts work was made or is important to people.
nodes.minimum_width: Student gives one reason for why a particular arts work exists or matters ('it tells a story', 'it's for celebrations', 'it teaches us something').
nodes.typical_width: Students discuss why arts works are created and shared — for celebrations, for communication, to express feelings, to teach — and connect these purposes to specific examples they have encountered.
wider: Students explore how drama and storytelling are used in their local First Nations community context to carry cultural knowledge and connection to Country/Place
Students compare why a familiar community arts event (e.g. a school performance, cultural celebration) exists and what it means to the people involved

response_modes.reason: Use concrete examples and guided questions ('Why do you think people made this?', 'What did it make people feel?') to scaffold simple causal reasoning about purpose.

success_criteria: Student gives at least one reason why an arts work or experience is important to people
Student connects the reason to a specific example from their experience
